title: Medical Clinic Rates: What Outpatient Suite Cleaning Costs Per Sq Ft and Per Month
seoTitle: Medical Clinic Rates: Outpatient Suite Cleaning Cost Per Sq Ft & Month
metaDescription: Medical clinic rates for outpatient suite cleaning: $0.07-$0.20 per sq ft per visit, restroom and exam room math, frequency tables, and a calculator CTA.
excerpt: Outpatient clinics pay more per square foot than standard offices because exam rooms, patient restrooms, and nightly disinfection add labor minutes. This guide shows the per-visit rate bands, the monthly math at 4.333 weeks, and how frequency and flooring move the final number.
quickAnswer: Most US medical clinics and outpatient suites pay $0.12-$0.20 per sq ft per visit under 2,500 sq ft and $0.09-$0.15 per sq ft between 2,500 and 9,999 sq ft, before restroom and flooring adjustments. A typical 4,500 sq ft family practice cleaned five nights a week lands around $7,900-$13,200 per month for the base scope, plus $15-$30 per restroom per visit. Clinics above 10,000 sq ft drop to $0.07-$0.12 per sq ft per visit but usually need daily service, so total monthly spend still climbs.

blocks.text: Why clinic square footage costs more than office square footage

A standard Class B office is mostly open carpet, private offices, and one or two restroom cores. A medical clinic or outpatient suite packs the same footprint with exam rooms, a lab or draw station, soiled utility closets, patient restrooms, and a waiting room that sees 60 to 150 visitors a day. Every one of those spaces has hard surfaces that must be cleaned and then disinfected with an EPA-registered product held wet for its full label dwell time. That is why the ISSA production benchmark of roughly 3,500 sq ft per hour for routine office cleaning falls to about 1,800-2,500 sq ft per hour in a clinic.

Vendors price that lost productivity into the per-square-foot rate. When you compare bids, the cheapest proposal often assumes office-speed production, which means either the crew skips dwell times or the vendor comes back in 90 days asking for a price increase. Knowing the realistic band protects you from both outcomes.
Per-visit rate bands by clinic size

The table below applies national per-visit square-foot rates to common outpatient formats, then multiplies by the frequency factor and visits per month (4.333 weeks per month). The figures cover the base nightly scope: trash and sharps-adjacent waste staging (not regulated medical waste hauling), hard-surface disinfection, floor care, and patient-area restocking. Restrooms are priced separately in the next section.

blocks.title: Minimum visit charge
blocks.text: Small suites under 1,000 sq ft rarely price on square footage alone. Expect a minimum of $90-$135 per visit because the vendor still has to dispatch a crew, carry a full disinfectant kit, and log the visit. If the square-foot math comes in below that floor, the minimum applies.
Restroom density: the line item clinics underestimate

Clinics typically carry one restroom for every 1,200-1,800 sq ft, compared with one for every 4,000-6,000 sq ft in a general office. Patient restrooms also double as specimen collection rooms, which means pass-through cabinets, grab bars, and baby changing stations that all need disinfection. Most vendors price restrooms at $15-$30 per restroom per visit on top of the square-foot rate.

items: 4,500 sq ft clinic with 4 restrooms, 5x/week: 4 x $15-$30 x 21.65 visits = $1,299-$2,598 per month.
2,000 sq ft practice with 2 restrooms, 3x/week: 2 x $15-$30 x 13 visits = $390-$780 per month.
12,000 sq ft suite with 9 restrooms, 5x/week: 9 x $15-$30 x 21.65 visits = $2,923-$5,846 per month.
Specimen restrooms with pass-through doors should sit at the top of the band because of the extra fixture surfaces.

blocks.text: Most clinics run sheet vinyl or VCT in clinical areas and carpet tile in administrative offices, which puts them in the mixed category with a 1.05 multiplier. All-VCT clinics use a 1.04 multiplier and need periodic burnishing; ceramic tile in procedure rooms or restrooms pushes toward 1.12 because grout lines trap bioburden. Waiting rooms take the heaviest wheel traffic from wheelchairs, walkers, and strollers, so build a quarterly deep floor program into the contract at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month amortized.

blocks.text: Recommended weekly frequency for outpatient suites

Frequency is driven by patient days, not square footage. A clinic that sees patients Monday through Friday needs five nightly visits; anything less leaves exam tables, door hardware, and restroom fixtures contaminated for a full clinical day. Practices that run Saturday hours should add a sixth visit or a weekend day porter. Monthly or biweekly service, which carries a 1.16-1.28 multiplier, only fits administrative-only suites with no patient contact.

items.name: Count patient days per week
items.text: Match nightly visits to clinical days. Five patient days means 21.65 visits per month at the 0.90 multiplier.

items.name: Separate clinical and admin square footage
items.text: Admin offices and billing areas can drop to 2x or 3x weekly while exam and patient zones stay nightly, which trims cost without touching infection control.

items.name: Add day porter coverage for high-volume waiting rooms
items.text: Urgent care and pediatric clinics often add a 2-4 hour midday porter at $35-$65 per hour for restroom checks and spill response.

items.name: Lock in periodic tasks
items.text: Schedule carpet extraction, VCT scrub-and-recoat, and high dusting of vents on a quarterly calendar inside the contract so they are not billed as surprise extras.

blocks.text: Supplies and chemicals that drive consumable cost

Clinic crews burn through disinfectant faster than office crews. A refillable bucket of EPA List N wipes such as CloroxPro Clorox Disinfecting Wipes (700-count, bleach-free) handles high-touch points like exam room door levers, keyboards on rolling carts, and check-in counters where spray-and-wipe would leave overspray on paper charts. Floors in exam corridors respond best to a neutral pH 7 no-rinse concentrate like Zep Neutral pH Industrial Floor Cleaner diluted at 1:128, which protects VCT finish from the alkaline residue that dulls it. For breakroom microwaves and the concrete entry at loading or ambulance doors, a phosphate-free biodegradable degreaser like Simple Green Pro HD keeps grease off without corroding fixtures. If you want the vendor to supply paper and soap, add $0.012-$0.025 per sq ft per visit.

blocks.title: Regulated medical waste is not janitorial scope
blocks.text: Sharps containers and red-bag waste are handled by a licensed medical waste hauler under state rules. Janitorial crews should never consolidate or transport red bags. Confirm the bid explicitly excludes RMW handling so you are not paying for a service the vendor cannot legally perform.
How to read a clinic cleaning bid

Ask every vendor to show square footage, rate per sq ft per visit, visits per month at 4.333 weeks, restroom count, and each add-on as separate lines. A lump-sum monthly number hides whether the vendor sized labor for clinic production rates. Also request the planned crew hours per night: a 4,500 sq ft clinic should show roughly 2-2.5 labor hours per visit, and a bid showing 1.2 hours is a red flag for skipped dwell times.

Plug your clinic's square footage, restroom count, flooring mix, and patient days into the Office Cleaning Cost Calculator, then line up vendor proposals side by side in the Quote Comparator to spot under-staffed bids.

faqs.q: How do vendors convert a weekly clinic schedule into a monthly invoice?
faqs.a: They multiply visits per week by 4.333 weeks per month. Five nights a week becomes 21.65 visits, three nights becomes 13 visits. A per-visit cost of $400 at five nights works out to about $8,660 per month. Contracts that bill a flat 20 visits per month undercount by more than one visit and the vendor usually recovers it elsewhere.

faqs.q: Should a clinic cleaning contractor carry special insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. Require a certificate of insurance (COI) naming your practice or landlord as additional insured, with general liability of at least $1 million per occurrence, workers compensation, and a janitorial or employee dishonesty bond. Many health systems also require professional or pollution liability when crews handle disinfectants in clinical spaces.

faqs.q: Does OSHA require training for clinic cleaning crews?
faqs.a: Crews with reasonably anticipated exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials fall under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030), which requires annual training and the offer of hepatitis B vaccination. The Hazard Communication Standard also requires Safety Data Sheets on site for every chemical the crew uses. Ask for training logs before the contract starts.

faqs.q: Is a green-certified cleaning program realistic in a clinic?
faqs.a: Partly. Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice products work well for glass, general surfaces, and floors in admin areas, but clinical surfaces still need an EPA-registered disinfectant with a claim for the pathogens your practice sees. A good vendor runs both: green cleaners for routine soil, registered disinfectants for exam and restroom surfaces.

faqs.q: What is usually excluded from a base clinic cleaning scope?
faqs.a: Common exclusions include regulated medical waste removal, instrument or equipment sterilization, cleaning inside medical devices, blood spill response beyond the initial absorbent cleanup, exterior windows, and carpet extraction outside the quarterly schedule. Get the exclusion list in writing so nothing surprises you at the first invoice.
